senses.en: a group of people who share the same language, culture and origins
examples: Viet Nam has 54 **ethnic groups**.
Each **ethnic group** has its own costume and festivals.
The Tay are the largest **ethnic group** in the north.

forms.en: connected with a group that shares a culture and origin
forms.ex: **Ethnic** costumes are worn at the festival.

senses.en: an ethnic group that is small in number compared with the main group in a country
examples: Many **ethnic minorities** live in the mountains.
The school teaches children from three **ethnic minorities**.
**Ethnic minority** languages are taught in some provinces.

ethnic minority.note: Opposite of *majority*. The plural is *minorit**ies*** — change *y* to *ies*.

senses.en: the largest part of a group; more than half
examples: The **majority** of people here are farmers.
The Kinh are the **majority** in Viet Nam.
A **majority** of students voted for the trip.

majority.note: Opposite: **minority**. With *the majority of + plural noun*, the verb is usually plural: *the majority of students **are** …*

senses.en: a way of behaving that a group of people has followed for a long time
examples: It is a **custom** to give lucky money at Tet.
Every village has its own **customs**.
Taking off your shoes indoors is a local **custom**.

senses.en: the place at a border or airport where officials check what you are bringing in
examples: We waited an hour to get through **customs**.
You must declare it at **customs**.

custom.note: A **custom** is what a group does; a *habit* is what one person does. Compare *tradition*, which is usually older and passed down through generations.

senses.en: the clothes worn by people of a particular place, period or group, especially at a special event
examples: The dancers wore traditional **costume**.
Each ethnic group has its own colourful **costume**.
She made a **costume** for the school play.

costume.note: **Costume** is special or traditional clothing, not everyday clothes — for those use *clothes*. Careful with the spelling: cos-**tume**, not *custom*.

senses.en: a house built on tall posts above the ground or above water
examples: Many ethnic groups live in **stilt houses**.
The **stilt house** keeps the family dry in the rainy season.
We climbed a wooden ladder into the **stilt house**.

forms.en: one of the long posts a building stands on

senses.en: one of a series of flat steps cut into a hillside so that crops can be grown on it
examples: The **terraced fields** of Sa Pa are famous.
Rice is grown on **terraced fields** in the mountains.
The **terraced fields** look like giant steps.

forms.en: a flat level area cut into a slope
forms.ex: Each **terrace** holds a few centimetres of water.

senses.en: the traditions, buildings and culture a country has had for many years and still values
examples: Ha Long Bay is a World **Heritage** Site.
Folk songs are part of our cultural **heritage**.
The village is proud of its **heritage**.

heritage.note: Uncountable — never *heritages*. Stress the first syllable: **HER**-i-tage.

senses.en: a set of actions always performed in the same way, especially as part of a ceremony
examples: The **ritual** is performed at the start of the harvest.
Lighting incense is an important **ritual**.
The wedding follows an ancient **ritual**.

senses.en: something you always do in the same way, out of habit
examples: Sunday lunch with my grandparents is a family **ritual**.
Coffee at seven is his morning **ritual**.

senses.en: a traditional song of a particular region, usually passed on by being sung rather than written down
examples: She sang an old **folk song** at the festival.
**Folk songs** tell the story of the village.
My grandmother taught me three **folk songs**.

forms.en: traditional, belonging to ordinary people of a region

senses.en: a tall tropical plant with hard hollow stems, used for building and making things
examples: Baskets are woven from **bamboo**.
The stilt house is built of **bamboo** and wood.
**Bamboo** grows very quickly.

senses.en: to make cloth or baskets by passing threads or strips over and under each other
examples: The women **weave** cloth on wooden looms.
She learned to **weave** baskets from her mother.
This scarf was **woven** by hand.

forms.ex: She is the best **weaver** in the village.

senses.en: a container made of thin strips of wood, bamboo or cane woven together
examples: She carried the fruit in a bamboo **basket**.
The **baskets** are woven by hand.
Put the eggs in that **basket**.

senses.en: a round metal disc that makes a deep ringing sound when you hit it
examples: The **gong** is played at village ceremonies.
**Gong** culture in the Central Highlands is a World Heritage tradition.
He struck the **gong** three times.

senses.en: a large natural hole in the side of a hill or under the ground
examples: Son Doong is the largest **cave** in the world.
Early people lived in **caves**.
We explored a **cave** near the village.

senses.en: being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else
senses.vi: độc đáo, độc nhất vô nhị
examples: Each ethnic group has its own **unique** costume.
The festival is **unique** to this province.
Every fingerprint is **unique**.

unique.note: Because it means *the only one*, careful writers avoid *very unique* or *quite unique* — something is either unique or it isn't. Pronounced /juˈniːk/: yoo-**NEEK**.

senses.en: very different from each other; of many different kinds
examples: Viet Nam is culturally very **diverse**.
The country has a **diverse** range of landscapes.
Our class is **diverse** — six languages are spoken.

forms.en: the fact of including many different kinds

senses.en: following ideas, customs or methods that have existed for a long time
examples: They wore **traditional** costumes for the festival.
Weaving is a **traditional** craft in this village.
**Traditional** music is played on the gong.

forms.en: a belief or custom passed from one generation to the next
forms.ex: It is a **tradition** to visit relatives at Tet.

forms.en: in the way that has been usual for a long time

senses.en: a large building that belongs to a whole village and is used for meetings, festivals and ceremonies
senses.vi: nhà rông, nhà sinh hoạt cộng đồng
examples: The Bahnar build the tallest **communal house** in the middle of the village.
Every decision about the harvest is made in the **communal house**.
Visitors are welcomed at the **communal house** before they go to anyone's home.

communal house.note: Two words, and the stress falls on the second syllable of *communal*: /kəˈmjuːnl/. It is a building for the whole community, not a house anybody lives in — so *my communal house* is almost never right.

senses.en: the animals a farm keeps for work, food or wool — cattle, buffaloes, pigs, goats, sheep
examples: Her family's **livestock** graze on the hillside above the village.
In the dry season there is not much grass for the **livestock**.
Under the floor of the stilt house they used to keep tools and **livestock**.

livestock.note: No plural *-s*: ❌ *many livestocks* → ✅ **a lot of livestock**. The word looks singular but takes a plural verb: *the livestock **are** in the field*. It does not cover chickens and ducks — those are *poultry*.

senses.en: to keep and feed animals so that they grow, usually in order to sell them or use them
examples: Most families here **raise** pigs and chickens behind the house.
The Jrai **raise** buffaloes, and in some villages elephants too.
My aunt **raised** goats for twenty years before she moved to town.

senses.en: to lift something to a higher position
examples: **Raise** your hand if you have visited a stilt house.
They **raised** the roof beam with ropes and a dozen pairs of hands.

forms.en: the work of keeping and feeding animals
forms.ex: Cattle **raising** is the main work of the village.

raise.note: *Raise* always takes an object — you raise *something*. The verb for going up by itself is *rise*: *the river **rises** in the rainy season*, but *they **raise** the roof*.

senses.en: the work of looking after a garden — planting, watering, weeding and cutting back
examples: My grandmother spends every morning **gardening** behind the kitchen.
**Gardening** is the first job the younger children are given.
He grew fond of **gardening** after his family moved to the countryside.

gardening.note: English says **do the gardening**, not *make the gardening* and not *do gardening work*. Note the spelling: one *d*, and no *e* before the *-ing*.

senses.en: the top layer of the earth that plants grow in
examples: The **soil** on a steep slope is thin and washes away in heavy rain.
Coffee grows well in the red **soil** of the Central Highlands.
They spread ash over the field to feed the **soil**.

soil.note: Uncountable: ❌ *many soils* → ✅ **a lot of soil**. *Soil* is what you grow things in; *ground* is what you stand on; *land* is an area you own or farm. Rice grows in the *soil*, on someone's *land*.

senses.en: to have a view down over something, because of standing higher than it
examples: Their stilt house **overlooks** the terraced fields.
The communal house **overlooked** the whole valley from the top of the hill.
We ate on a balcony **overlooking** the river.

senses.en: to fail to notice something, or to decide not to punish a small mistake
examples: It is easy to **overlook** the smallest groups when you count fifty-four.
The teacher **overlooked** one spelling mistake and marked the rest.

overlook.note: The two senses are almost opposites — one is *see very well*, the other is *not see at all*. What follows the verb tells you which: a house *overlooks* a place, a person *overlooks* a mistake.

senses.en: a fire burning in the open, with no stove or chimney around it
examples: An **open fire** burns in the middle of the kitchen floor all winter.
The family sits round the **open fire**, and guests are seated nearest it.
Sticky rice cooked over an **open fire** tastes of smoke.

open fire.note: The preposition after it is **over** for cooking (*cook over an open fire*) and **round** or **around** for sitting. Not the same as a *fireplace*, which is built into a wall.

senses.en: a figure of a person or an animal, carved from wood or stone or cast in metal
examples: Wooden **statues** stand round the grave, one for each member of the family.
The **statue** by the gate was cut from a single trunk.
He carves a small **statue** of a bird for every grandchild.

statue.note: Say /ˈstætʃuː/ — the *t* sounds like the *ch* in *church*, not like a plain /t/. Do not confuse it with *status* /ˈsteɪtəs/, which means a position or rank.

senses.en: a musical instrument shaped like a tube, which you play by blowing across or into a hole
examples: He cut a **flute** from a length of bamboo and played us a tune.
The **flute** and the gong are played together at the harvest festival.
She has been learning the **flute** since she was seven.

forms.en: a person who plays the flute
forms.ex: The **flautist** stood at the front of the group.

flute.note: Instruments take **the** after *play*: *play **the** flute*, *play **the** gong*. Sports do not: *play football*. And it is *play the flute*, never *blow the flute*.

senses.en: an object made for producing music, such as a flute, a gong or a guitar
examples: The đàn tính is the **musical instrument** most closely tied to the Tay.
Every child in the village learns at least one **musical instrument**.
Their **musical instruments** are made from bamboo, wood and bronze.

musical instrument.note: Countable, so it takes *a* and a plural *-s*: *two **musical instruments***. *Musical* here means *for making music*; a *musical person* is something else — someone good at music.

senses.en: a traditional dance of a particular people, learnt from older dancers rather than at a school
examples: Múa sạp is the **folk dance** everyone knows, and the bamboo poles do half the work.
The village performs three **folk dances** at the spring festival.
She learnt the **folk dance** from her grandmother, step by step.

folk dance.note: *Folk* /fəʊk/ has a silent *l* — say it like *joke* with an *f*. The same word builds *folk song*, *folk music* and *folk tale*, and in all of them it means *belonging to ordinary people, passed down by ear*.

senses.en: a kind of rice whose grains hold together after cooking, used for festival food and cakes
examples: **Sticky rice** dyed five colours is served at Tay weddings.
She steams the **sticky rice** in a wooden pot over an open fire.
Bánh chưng is made of **sticky rice**, pork and green beans.

sticky rice.note: Uncountable, like *rice* itself: ❌ *two sticky rices* → ✅ **two bowls of sticky rice**. The colours come from leaves and roots boiled with the grains, not from anything artificial.

senses.en: a part of something that you notice, and that makes it different from other things of its kind
examples: The tall roof is the first **feature** you notice about a Rong house.
Each group's costume has **features** that nobody else's has.
One useful **feature** of a stilt house is the dry space underneath.

senses.en: to include something as an important part
senses.vi: có, trưng bày, làm nổi bật
examples: The exhibition **features** costumes from all fifty-four groups.
Their folk songs often **feature** a bamboo flute.

forms.ex: The **featured** photograph shows a terraced field at dawn.

feature.note: In the plural, *someone's features* means the parts of their face. *The features of the house* is fine; *the features of my sister* means her eyes, nose and mouth.
